implementation: Bounded unaligned 32-bit ordinary-memory copy/move/fill; strings use sequential byte checks with four-byte loop unrolling. No speculative word reads past NUL, no DSP/NEON instructions.
scope: Existing resident Flash functions vs matched scalar/candidate SRAM APP kernels. Includes same wrapper dispatch; not a resident replacement or end-to-end throughput claim. strcmp/strnlen private Flash addresses are qualification-only, guarded by exact firmware CRC, public anchors and code bytes.

measurement.compiler: xPack ARM GCC 14.2.1, wrappers noipa/16-byte aligned/-Os
measurement.cycles_include: Identical APP function-pointer loop and return checksum. Median of seven samples, then median across three runs; scalar_sram and candidate_sram share code placement.
measurement.transport: Public FILE_WRITE to bounded base64 TEXT files, read over CDC; own files removed.
measurement.private_address_guards: Sealed ELF must reproduce BIN exactly; identity and full resident CRC matched before installation; public memcpy/memcmp anchors matched in APP; strcmp/strnlen code prefixes matched each report.

decisions.memset: Promising on blocks >=16; 512-byte word version is 5.47..7.57 times faster than matched SRAM byte control. Tiny-path overhead needs tuning before global qualification.
decisions.memmove: Promising on blocks >=16; 512-byte overlapping shifts (excluding self) improve 2.32..3.72 times against matched SRAM byte control. Forward and backward correctness passed; tiny rightward overlaps regress.
decisions.strlen: Byte unrolling improves matched SRAM control about 1.42 times on long strings, but measured candidate is slower than existing resident Flash strlen there. Keep resident until matched Flash qualification.
decisions.strnlen: Byte unrolling improves matched SRAM control about 1.64 times on long strings; measured advantage over existing Flash code is only about 6%, and the bound-zero path regresses. Low priority.
decisions.strcmp: Reject this four-byte unrolling: equal and late-difference cases are slower than both scalar SRAM and existing Flash. First-byte mismatch gives no gain over SRAM scalar.
decisions.strncmp: Byte unrolling improves SRAM control about 1.23 times on long equal strings, but loses to existing resident Flash on those cases. Keep existing code.
decisions.memcpy: Bounded word implementation is already globally committed in main by 0e139bc6a with separate matched Flash/end-to-end qualification. This APP reconfirms its SRAM advantage; no further production memcpy change.
